title: Every registered wrapper writes through the existing discipline and adds nothing to it
statement: Each registered creation, mutation, activation and stage-attestation tool performs its write through the existing locked, atomic, validated implementation rather than reaching the filesystem itself, and every wrapper - read or write - resolves the content root through the shared resolver rather than deriving one. A wrapper adds only the Pi-facing schema and the rendering of a result: no validation rule, no id allocation, no trace rule and no write path is restated in it. Every result is structured, a refusal is returned as data rather than thrown as prose, and neither carries a credential, a credential-derived value or an absolute user path.
notes: ⚠️ NARROWED TO TSK-0044. This criterion accepted TSK-0044 AND TSK-0045, which do not depend on each other, so neither could be finished without the other's work also being done - and its wording is about mutation wrappers, which are TSK-0044's, while TSK-0045's adapters mostly write no planning content at all. TSK-0045 now has its own criterion for what its adapters must do. ⚠️ THE WRAPPER IS A BOUNDARY, NOT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION. Everything it calls already exists in `lib/` with the lock, the atomic write, the schema validation and the id allocator behind it. A wrapper that re-derived the content root, or re-checked a rule, would be a second answer to a question that already has one - which is how the two drift apart without either being obviously wrong.
